source: Planted for wf-intake on the average seed: one line two readers would grade differently.

request.text: average([]) gives NaN and it ended up as NaN in an invoice total last week. An empty list should average to 0.

issue.title: average([]) should be 0
issue.problem: average([]) returns NaN, because it divides by the length 0.
issue.outcome: average of an empty list is 0, and the fix is covered by a test.
expect: test/math.test.js has a test that calls average([]) and expects 0, and npm test passes

proofs.line: test/math.test.js has a test that calls average([]) and expects 0, and npm test passes

trap: Line 2 has no fixed meaning: one reader passes a build that returns NaN for ['a'], another fails it.
must_catch: Line 2 FAILs as ambiguous, naming two readings.
